# react

React 19 bindings of omai-render. Figures: `Chart` (an ECharts option), `SceneView`, `Scene3DView` and `StructureView`, in a `FigureFrame` (fixed size, expand, export) or a `FigureGrid`; typeset and live maths (`Tex`, `Equation`, `Derivation`); `ContingencyTable` and `ThresholdExplorer`; playback (`usePlayback`, `useLiveRun` and the `Player` over their controller); the colour-mode theme (`ThemeProvider`, `useColourMode`) and the pixel ratio hosts magnify figures at (`PixelRatioProvider`). Subfolders: `session` (`useSession`, `SessionPlayer`, `SessionPanels`: run a method live and draw it), `controls` (inputs and controls generated from a `Space`), `interaction` (draggable overlays on a figure) and `views` (`ExpositionView` and one view per exposition record kind).

## react/controls

Form controls for figures and demos, in plain React and Tailwind over the `--wb-*` tokens. Inputs: `NumberField`, `Select`, `Choice`, `Toggle`, `SeedInput`, `ColumnOrder`. Generated from an engine `Space`: `SpaceControls` (options a rule rules out drawn disabled), `SpaceSettings` and `SettingsButton` (a modal applied on confirm), `ModelSelector` (a union's options with a settings popover each) and `SlotVariants` (the options of a slot compared at once). Choosing data: `DatasetPicker` and `DatasetSelector` with `useDataset`, `EnvironmentSelector`. Layout: `ControlPanel` and `ControlLayout` put controls beside a figure; `FigurePanel`, `PanelsStrip` and `usePanels` let a page fold or hide its figures. Validity rules read from the option tables' properties, and the rest of the rules behind the controls, are pure modules.

## react/interaction

Interaction overlays laid over any figure through a projection between data and pixels: get the projection of a `Chart` with `useChartProjection`, stack the figure and an `InteractionOverlay` with `Overlaid`, and put tools inside: `DraggablePoints` (kept where a `Constraint` allows), `DraggableLine`, `DraggableRect`, `Brush`, `Probe` and `NearestHover`. `useLinkState` reads state shared between linked figures, and `useHeldKeys` captures the keys a game-like figure reads.

## react/session

Sessions in React. `useSession` runs a method live (`useSessions` runs several variants of it in step under one producer, `variantsOfSlot` makes one variant per option of a slot) and gives a live handle; `SessionPlayer` plays it; a layout (`Panel`, in `layout.ts`) declares what to draw and `SessionPanels` draws it over the tape (overlaying the variants of a comparison on curves and sweeps, and drawing the rest side by side), with `NarrativeView` for a session told in pages and `TapeView` for the generic viewer of everything a tape holds. All share one step cursor (`useStepCursor`) that charts of the tape move on click. `SessionExport` exports a page and `useTape` replays a saved tape. The rows panel's channels (values, sizes, marks, regions, a focus), the curve families (many runs, bands, truth lines, log axes, events, interval strips) and the variants of a slot are pure modules beside the panels.

- structure `layout.ts` (file): Every panel kind a layout can declare: `{ kind: 'curves', paths: ['loss'] }` `src/react/session/layout.ts:1` `omai-render/react`

## react/views

React components for exposition records: `ExpositionView` picks the standard view of any record by its `kind`, and each kind has its own view to use directly (`DecisionSurfaceView`, `PathView`, `TreeView`, `CurvesView`, `ClusteringPlayer`, `AttributionView`, `GroupReportView`, `CalibrationView`, `EpisodeView` and more), each one figure in a figure frame with any player beneath it. All take the `record` and, optionally, a `figure`, a `title`, a `caption` and a `filename` for export.
